title: First Act Turning Point (16-22 minutes):
use_cases: Use when structuring a screenplay to signify the shift from exploration to conflict
Implement when the protagonist realizes a threat can no longer be ignored
Configure when bridging the gap between introductory exposition and the main rising action
Use when establishing a irrevocable commitment to the central mission or goal
content:
The point of no return — this is when the protagonist(s) realise(s) they’re in big trouble. It is often the first full-on encounter with the evil, or at least a moment when they realise that they are in danger and there is no going back with regards to the situation they find themselves in. Now there is no denying that bad shit is going down. It can’t be ignored, it has to be faced!

Example: In “Alien” (1979), the facehugger attaches to Kane, forcing the crew to take action. They are now dealing with an alien threat. This event ends their exploratory mission and begins their survival horror journey, leading straight into the beginning of Act Two, where the crew returns to the Nostromo with Kane, and actively tries to understand and combat the alien threat.
